# Physical tables

Every table a full installation creates: 1,240 tables holding 13,518 columns. This is observed from a running installation carrying every capability package, not inferred from a definition, so it records what the storage layer actually contains.

For each table the entity it stores is named where one exists. Tables with no entity are either association tables implementing a many-to-many relation, or tables belonging to an abstract construct that has no records of its own.

Storage types are given in the form the database reports, followed by their meaning in words, because a rebuild on a different storage engine must preserve the meaning rather than the spelling.

## Summary

| Measure | Count |
|---|---|
| Tables | 1,240 |
| Columns | 13,518 |
| Tables backing an entity | 803 |
| Association tables for many-to-many relations | 422 |
| Indexes | 2,933 |
| Foreign keys | 4,575 |
